memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The LORD said to Moses, 'Bring Aaron and his sons, their garments, the anointing oil, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams and the basket containing bread made without yeast, and gather the entire assembly at the entrance to the tent of meeting.'" - Lev 8:1-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Seven chapters of instruction end, and now something happens. God has explained the offerings; here He begins appointing the men who will handle them.

Notice the last phrase: gather the entire assembly. This ordination was not a private ceremony behind a curtain. The whole nation stood and watched.

There was wisdom in that. Everyone saw exactly how Aaron became high priest — that he did not appoint himself, did not campaign for it, and did not inherit it by ambition. God chose him, and Israel witnessed it. No one could later claim the priesthood had been seized.

Hebrews makes this point about spiritual authority generally: No one takes this honour on himself, but he receives it when called by God, just as Aaron was (Heb 5:4). And then it says the same of Christ: So Christ also did not take on himself the glory of becoming a high priest. God said to him, "You are my Son" (Heb 5:5).

Genuine spiritual authority is received, never grasped. Whenever someone in the church takes a position by force of personality or manoeuvring, something is out of order.

Notice too what Moses is told to bring: garments, oil, a bull, two rams, bread. God supplies everything the calling requires.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I seeking a role for myself that God has not given me?
2. Where has God clearly placed me, and am I serving faithfully there?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep me from grasping at positions You have not given. Help me serve faithfully where You have actually placed me. Amen.
